constitutive_assumptions: Linear elastic behavior under small deformations and small strains.
Specially orthotropic layers whose principal material axes coincide with the plate coordinate axes.
Kirchhoff-Love kinematic assumptions within each individual layer, assuming zero out-of-plane transverse shear strain internally within individual lamellae.
Interlayer partial interaction modeled via linear elastic shear springs where transverse shear stress is directly proportional to relative tangential slip displacements across interfaces.
Zero transverse normal separation or peeling between layers (transverse deflection w is uniform through the thickness).

Homogeneous individual layers of uniform thickness with rectangular cross-sections, causing stretching-bending coupling (Bi) and translational-rotational inertia coupling (I1,i) of individual layers to vanish.
Plate global coordinate system origin chosen to eliminate laminate-level stretching-bending coupling.
In-plane compressive edge loads distributed among layers proportionally to their relative axial stiffness.
control_variables: Simply supported edge boundary conditions on all four plate edges.
Total laminate thickness kept constant when varying layer count.
Uniform individual layer thickness for identical layer cases and equal ply thickness in cross-ply cases.
Fixed material properties for validation benchmarks (e.g., Al 2024-T3 sheet properties: E = 70.15 GPa, G = 27.6 GPa, nu = 0.33, rho = 2780 kg/m3; cross-ply properties: G12 = 0.5*E_perp, nu12 = 0.25).
dependent_variables: Critical buckling load parameter (mono-axial and bi-axial).
Natural vibration frequencies and frequency parameters.
Buckling and vibration mode shapes (number of half-waves m1, m2).
Relative interfacial shear slips between adjacent layers.

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Interfacial shear slip and partial interaction between constituent layers can be modeled analytically via an equivalent shear spring model relating interface shear stresses to tangential slip discontinuities.
Structural stiffness, critical buckling loads, and natural frequencies degrade systematically from classical perfect-bonding plate predictions as interlayer shear interaction decreases.
For completely debonded/frictionless layers (zero interlayer shear stiffness), the critical buckling load decreases by a factor of 1/n^2 relative to the perfectly bonded ideal laminate.
The sensitivity of mechanical performance (buckling resistance and vibration frequencies) to the level of interlayer interaction increases markedly as the number of constituent layers increases.
3-D finite element analysis of multi-layer panels bonded with soft adhesive films demonstrates that modulating interfacial shear modulus directly alters natural frequencies across multiple modes.
Variations in the interlayer shear interaction modulus can alter the sequence of vibration modes, causing mode shifting relative to perfectly bonded composite laminates.

future_work: Extending LPCPT to incorporate shear-deformable kinematic models (from Mindlin-Reissner to higher-order shear deformation theories) for internal transverse shear deformation within individual layers.
Developing laminated partial-composite shell theories based on diverse kinematic models.
Applying LPCPT formulations to other material classes, such as functionally graded materials (FGMs).
Extending analytical and numerical solutions to different boundary conditions, general loading scenarios, and wider static and dynamic problems.
independent_variables: Interlayer shear interaction/slip modulus (k and dimensionless k).
In-plane compressive loading type (mono-axial x, mono-axial y, bi-axial) and load intensity factors (xi1, xi2).
Material orthotropy ratio (E_parallel / E_perp) and stacking sequence.
Inclusion or exclusion of rotary inertia effects.
limitations_inferred: The model assumes equal transverse deflection across all layers and does not capture out-of-plane normal separation, opening, or peeling stresses between layers.
Linear elastic spring behavior is assumed for interlayer shear slip, neglecting nonlinear elastoplastic or viscoelastic interface kinematics.
Navier-type closed-form analytical solutions are restricted to rectangular plates with simply supported boundary conditions.
The model is formulated under linear elastic small-deflection kinematics and does not account for geometric nonlinearities or large deflections.
No robotic applications, soft robotic systems, or active variable-stiffness mechanisms are evaluated or implemented.
limitations_stated_by_authors: The theory specifically focuses on partial-composite shear slip imperfection and excludes other forms of interfacial bonding defects such as cracks, delamination, geometric gaps, or uneven bonding.
Individual layers are governed by classical Kirchhoff-Love plate kinematics, neglecting internal transverse shear deformation within individual lamellae.
Stretching-bending uncoupling requires symmetric layups or placing the global coordinate origin at a specific transversal centroid.

The hyperbolic analytical formulation for an arbitrary layer number n requires identical layer geometries and orthotropic properties; non-identical multilayers require direct algebraic determinant solutions of order (2n+1).
Through-thickness stress asymmetry in extremely thick plates cannot be captured by this or other plate/shell theories.
Experimental techniques for determining interlayer interaction moduli were reviewed from literature but not performed within this study.
main_results: Formulated the Laminated Partial-Composite Plate Theory (LPCPT) extending CLPT to account for interlayer shear slip using Hamilton's energy principle.
Derived general exact analytical solutions for buckling under mono- and bi-axial compression and free vibration for flexible n-layer plates with identical orthotropic layers.

Demonstrated that when the interlayer shear modulus is set to the equivalent transverse shear modulus (k = k*) and n approaches infinity, the asymptotic buckling solution exactly matches Reddy's higher-order shear deformation theory (HSDT) and closely matches 3-D elasticity.
Validated the analytical solutions against 3-D finite element analysis in Abaqus for 4- and 6-layer aluminum panels bonded with soft adhesives, showing strong agreement across natural frequencies.
Showed that structural stiffness, buckling loads, and natural frequencies degrade substantially as interlayer interaction decreases, with sensitivity scaling with layer count.

Demonstrated that the extent of interlayer interaction can trigger vibration mode shifting and that rotary inertia effects ('partial rotary inertia') become more pronounced as interlayer bonding increases.
modeling_methods: Laminated Partial-Composite Plate Theory (LPCPT) based on Kirchhoff-Love kinematics per layer.
Extended Hamilton's variational energy principle for governing equations and extended boundary conditions.
Shear spring interface model relating transverse shear stress to tangential slip discontinuities.
Navier-type double Fourier series combined with truncated polynomial displacement fields.
Coupled difference equation analytical scheme using hyperbolic functions (cosh, sinh) for arbitrary layer numbers.
Direct algebraic characteristic determinant method for non-identical multilayer plates.
3-D Finite Element Analysis (FEA) in Abaqus/CAE using continuum solid shell elements (CSS8) for plates and solid brick elements (C3D8R) for adhesive layers.
performance_metrics: Dimensionless critical buckling load parameter (Ncr = Ncr * a^2 / D_infinity or Ncr * b^2 / (pi^2 * D)).
Dimensionless natural frequency parameter (omega_bar = omega * a^2 * sqrt(rho_ell * hTot / D_infinity)).
Percentage discrepancy relative to 3-D elasticity theory and classical plate theory (CPT).
Buckling and vibration mode sequences and mode shifting indicators.
possible_gap_implications: The mathematical modeling of interlayer shear slip and its effect on flexural rigidity could potentially inform variable-stiffness mechanics (such as layer jamming) in soft robotics, but adapting it would require incorporating hyperelasticity, large deformations, and frictional/vacuum-driven contact mechanics not covered in this paper.

The analytical framework assumes perfect transverse cohesion (no normal peeling), which may limit its direct application to soft robotic grippers where interfacial peel failure or normal lift-off occurs under contact loading.
paper.research_objective: To introduce the Laminated Partial-Composite Plate Theory (LPCPT) as an extension of the classical laminated plate theory (CLPT) that incorporates interlayer partial-interaction shear slip via a shear spring model, derive the governing differential equations and extended classical boundary conditions, and develop exact analytical solution schemes for free vibrations and buckling of flexible n-layer plates under mono- and bi-axial compressive loads.
paper.research_problem: Conventional laminated plate theories rely on idealized kinematic continuity and perfect bonding assumptions, failing to capture the performance degradation caused by interlayer shear slip (as in structures with soft adhesives, discrete mechanical fasteners, or partial debonding), while existing layerwise models capable of capturing imperfect bonding suffer from high computational expense that scales poorly with layer count and lack general analytical solutions for flexible n-layer plates.
paper.title: Laminated Partially-Composite Plate Theory (LPCPT)—An extension of the classical laminated plate theory for flexible n-layer plates with partial interlayer interaction
